results.summary: Precomputed future Raffle clone address bypasses sponsorRecipient protocol-destination screening in createRaffle and later locks sponsorProceeds and sponsorPrize
results.malicious_actor: Any external EOA or contract acting as raffle sponsor
results.malicious_input_example: createRaffle(CreateRaffleParams({ sponsorRecipient: computeCreateAddress(address(factory), factoryNonce + 1), prizeToken: address(nft), prizeTokenId: 1, reserveEntries: 10, endTime: uint64(block.timestamp + 1 days) })) followed by a second createRaffle(...) call that deploys the sibling clone at sponsorRecipient
trigger_flow: packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:97 RaffleFactory.createRaffle - Sponsor calls createRaffle with params.sponsorRecipient set to the deterministic CREATE address of a future Raffle clone
packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:166 RaffleFactory._validateCreateParams - Checks isRaffle[params.sponsorRecipient], which is false because the future clone has not been deployed yet

packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:193 Raffle.initialize - Calls _isProtocolDestination(params.sponsorRecipient, params.prizeToken), which skips canonicalFactory.isRaffle(destination) because destination.code.length == 0

packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:106 RaffleFactory.createRaffle - A subsequent createRaffle call deploys a new ERC-1167 clone via Clones.clone(raffleImplementation) at that exact CREATE address and sets isRaffle[sponsorRecipient] = true

packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:380 Raffle.releaseSponsorProceeds / packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:404 Raffle.releaseSponsorPrize - _transferQuote reverts permanently with InvalidQuoteDestination(sponsorRecipient) because isRaffle[sponsorRecipient] is now true, while releaseSponsorPrize transfers the NFT into the sibling Raffle clone where it is permanently stranded
results.explanation: RaffleFactory.createRaffle deploys Raffle clones using Clones.clone(raffleImplementation) (CREATE), making every future clone address deterministically predictable from the factory address and account nonce. Both RaffleFactory._validateCreateParams (line 166) and Raffle._isProtocolDestination (lines 602-604) only check isRaffle[destination] against already-deployed clones. When a sponsor sets params.sponsorRecipient to the next clone's deterministic CREATE address, raffle creation succeeds. Once the next raffle is created on the factory, isRaffle[sponsorRecipient] becomes true and destination.code.length != 0. Thereafter, calling releaseSponsorProceeds() on the first raffle permanently reverts with InvalidQuoteDestination(sponsorRecipient) at Raffle.sol:565 (locking sponsorProceeds USDC in the contract), and calling releaseSponsorPrize() at Raffle.sol:404 transfers the prize NFT into the sibling Raffle clone, which has no rescue mechanism.

21.stub_explanation: This flow is a pure revert-guard path in RaffleFactory.createRaffle that atomically rolls back state changes when validation or post-transfer prize escrow verification fails.

22.stub_explanation: Raffle.receive() unconditionally reverts with DirectNativeTransfer(), preventing stray native currency from being locked in the contract without affecting VRF wrapper payments or refunds in requestDraw().

results.summary: Raffle.initialize accepts a not-yet-deployed sibling Raffle clone address as sponsorRecipient because _isProtocolDestination only queries isRaffle when destination.code.length != 0
results.malicious_actor: Raffle sponsor supplying RaffleInitParams via canonical RaffleFactory.createRaffle
results.malicious_input_example: RaffleInitParams with sponsorRecipient set to the deterministic CREATE address of a future RaffleFactory clone (where sponsorRecipient.code.length == 0 and isRaffle[sponsorRecipient] == false at initialization time)
trigger_flow: packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:109 RaffleFactory.createRaffle - Calls IRaffle(raffle).initialize with caller-supplied sponsorRecipient
packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:602 Raffle._isProtocolDestination - Skips canonicalFactory.isRaffle(destination) because destination.code.length == 0 before the future sibling clone is deployed
packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:198 Raffle.initialize - Persists sponsorRecipient in clone storage

packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:125 RaffleFactory.createRaffle - Subsequent raffle creation deploys a clone at sponsorRecipient and sets isRaffle[sponsorRecipient] = true, causing Raffle._transferQuote in releaseSponsorProceeds to revert with InvalidQuoteDestination and releaseSponsorPrize to strand the prize NFT inside the sibling clone
results.explanation: During Raffle.initialize, _isProtocolDestination(params.sponsorRecipient, params.prizeToken) only checks whether sponsorRecipient is a currently deployed and registered Raffle clone (destination.code.length != 0 && canonicalFactory.isRaffle(destination)). Because RaffleFactory uses deterministic CREATE via Clones.clone, a future clone address has code.length == 0 at initialization time and passes screening, but becomes a prohibited protocol destination (isRaffle == true) as soon as that future raffle is created. Once deployed, _transferQuote(sponsorRecipient, amount) in releaseSponsorProceeds() permanently reverts with InvalidQuoteDestination, and releaseSponsorPrize() transfers the prize NFT into the sibling Raffle clone where it cannot be recovered.

24.stub_explanation: This flow is a pure revert-guard path in Raffle.initialize that blocks re-initialization, non-factory callers, zero addresses, and currently registered protocol destinations.

results.summary: buyEntries allows minting tickets to a precomputed future Raffle clone address because _update and _safeMint see code.length == 0 before the sibling clone is deployed
results.malicious_actor: Any external EOA or contract purchasing raffle entries
results.malicious_input_example: buyEntries(computeCreateAddress(address(factory), factoryNonce), 1) followed by RaffleFactory.createRaffle(...) deploying a Raffle clone at recipient
trigger_flow: packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:209 Raffle.buyEntries - Caller invokes buyEntries(recipient, entryCount) with recipient set to a deterministic future Raffle clone CREATE address

packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:498 Raffle._update - Calls _isProtocolDestination(recipient, address(prizeToken)), which returns false because recipient.code.length == 0 and isRaffle[recipient] == false
packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:501 Raffle._update - Mints ticketId to recipient; ERC721Utils.checkOnERC721Received skips the onERC721Received callback because recipient.code.length == 0

packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol:106 RaffleFactory.createRaffle - Next raffle creation deploys a Raffle clone at recipient and sets isRaffle[recipient] = true, stranding the ticket in a Raffle contract that cannot transfer, redeem, or refund it
results.explanation: Raffle._update (line 498) screens ticket recipients via _isProtocolDestination(to, address(prizeToken)) to enforce the invariant that protocol contracts cannot own tickets and strand claims. However, _isProtocolDestination (lines 602-604) only queries canonicalFactory.isRaffle(to) when to.code.length != 0, and OpenZeppelin ERC721._safeMint skips onERC721Received when to.code.length == 0. Because RaffleFactory deploys clones at deterministic CREATE addresses via Clones.clone, a buyer can pass a not-yet-deployed Raffle clone address as recipient in buyEntries. Once that sibling Raffle clone is deployed by a subsequent createRaffle call, the ticket is owned by a Raffle clone (isRaffle[recipient] == true), which has no mechanism to transfer, redeem, or refund the ticket (and _transferQuote also rejects isRaffle addresses), permanently locking the prize or refund liability.

26.stub_explanation: This flow is a pure revert-guard path in Raffle.buyEntries that rejects purchases when the raffle is not Active, the sale has ended, entryCount is zero or overflows uint128, or the recipient is invalid.

27.stub_explanation: Raffle.requestDraw is protected by nonReentrant and _requestInFlight, validates the [endTime, drawRequestDeadline()) window and totalEntries > 0, pays the exact wrapper fee from msg.value, and atomically refunds only msg.value - paidPrice to msg.sender.

28.stub_explanation: This flow is a pure revert-guard path in Raffle.requestDraw that rolls back the transaction if preconditions, fee coverage, or caller refund acceptance fail.

29.stub_explanation: When status is Active and totalEntries == 0, Raffle.enableRefunds properly restricts pre-endTime cancellation to sponsor while allowing anyone to transition the empty raffle to Refunding at or after endTime.

30.stub_explanation: When status is Active and totalEntries != 0, Raffle.enableRefunds enforces block.timestamp >= drawRequestDeadline() (matching the exclusive cutoff in requestDraw) and safely moves unsettledPot into remainingRefundLiability.

31.stub_explanation: When status is Drawing, Raffle.enableRefunds enforces block.timestamp >= callbackDeadline() (matching the exclusive cutoff in fulfillRandomWords) and transitions the raffle to Refunding so buyers and the sponsor can recover their assets.

32.stub_explanation: This flow is a pure revert-guard path in Raffle.enableRefunds that prevents premature refund activation or transitions from terminal states.

33.stub_explanation: In Status.NftWon, Raffle.settleWinningTicket verifies that ticketId's stored range contains winningEntry (which is always in [1, totalEntries], excluding unminted [0, 0] ranges) and conserves unsettledPot across protocolFees (5% rounded down) and sponsorProceeds (remainder).

34.stub_explanation: In Status.CashWon, Raffle.settleWinningTicket verifies that ticketId's stored range contains winningEntry and conserves unsettledPot across protocolFees (5% rounded down), winnerProceeds (80% rounded down), and sponsorProceeds (remainder).

35.stub_explanation: This flow is a pure revert-guard path in Raffle.settleWinningTicket that blocks duplicate settlement, invalid statuses, and non-winning or unminted ticket IDs.

36.stub_explanation: In Status.NftWon, Raffle.redeemWinningTicket is nonReentrant, settles or verifies winningTicketId, checks msg.sender == ownerOf(ticketId), burns the ticket and sets winnerRedeemed/prizeClaimed before calling prizeToken.transferFrom, and verifies post-transfer ownership.

37.stub_explanation: In Status.CashWon, Raffle.redeemWinningTicket is nonReentrant, settles or verifies winningTicketId, checks msg.sender == ownerOf(ticketId), burns the ticket and zeroes winnerProceeds before transferring USDC via _transferQuote.

38.stub_explanation: This flow is a pure revert-guard path in Raffle.redeemWinningTicket that enforces single redemption, valid terminal status, winning ticket match, current ticket ownership, and prize delivery verification.

39.stub_explanation: Raffle.refundTickets is nonReentrant, bounds batch size to 1..100, verifies msg.sender == ownerOf(ticketId), and burns each ticket inside the loop before transferring aggregate entries * ENTRY_PRICE in USDC, preventing duplicate ticket IDs in a batch from double-claiming refunds.
